verdict.rationale: Notion can act as a shared context store across tools and agents. Its official MCP server lets clients such as Claude Code, Cursor and Codex read, create and update workspace content. The Agent APIs expose sessions with readable event history, and Skills pages hold reusable workflow instructions that any assistant can use. Webhooks and the REST API add real-time sync and broad read/write access, but continuity across a handoff is implied by these shared building blocks rather than shipped as a dedicated feature. Missing for 10: an explicit documented agent-to-agent or tool-to-tool handoff mechanism that guarantees context is preserved, and independent or hands-on corroboration of context continuity across handoffs.
